summary: The main article describes the use of a porphyrinic MOF, PCN-222, for the photocatalytic oxidative coupling of amines. It includes two tables detailing reaction optimization and substrate scope, one scheme illustrating the dual charge and energy transfer mechanism, and two figures providing ESR evidence for reaction intermediates.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Schematic illustration of LCCT and ET processes involved in PCN-222 for the selective oxidative coupling of amines under visible light irradiation.
items.description: This scheme illustrates the linker-to-cluster charge transfer (LCCT) and energy transfer (ET) pathways that enable the photocatalytic coupling of amines to imines.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Oxidative coupling of benzylamines under various conditions a
items.description: This table presents the optimization of reaction conditions, comparing PCN-222 with control experiments and its organic counterpart TPPCOOMe.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Photocatalytic oxidative coupling of various amines into imines a
items.description: This table explores the substrate scope of the reaction, showing the conversion and selectivity for various primary, secondary, and heterocyclic amines.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: (a) ESR detection of the electron transfer process in PCN-222. (b) ESR detection of O2 c 0 generation over PCN-222 trapped by DMPO. (c) The detection of hole-involved intermediates in PCN-222. (d) Hammett plot for the oxidation of benzylamine and its para -substituted derivatives photocatalyzed by PCN-222.
items.description: This figure provides experimental ESR data and a Hammett plot to support the proposed charge transfer mechanism and identify radical intermediates.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: (a) Proposed charge transfer process for the photocatalytic oxidative coupling of benzylamine over PCN-222, in which the complex HOMO constitution is simpli fi ed. (b) ESR spectra (light -dark di ff erence) of PCN-222 for the 1 O2 detection in the presence of 4oxo-TMP.
items.description: This figure details the proposed charge transfer mechanism and provides ESR evidence for the generation of singlet oxygen via energy transfer.
